title: Object
body:
[[Method]]
[[Javascript Objects]]

An **instance** of a [[Class]]. The class is the type, the object is the variable:

```c++
IntStack s;      // IntStack is the class, s is the object
s.push(4);
```

Same relationship as `struct Student` and `Student jones` in [[Structure]]: the definition
creates a type, not storage. Declaring the object is what reserves the memory and runs the
constructor.

An object bundles **state** (its data members) with **behaviour** (its [[Method]]s), which is
the difference from a plain struct and the whole of [[Encapsulation]]. Each object has its own
copy of the data; the methods are shared.

Objects are copied on assignment, on pass or return by value, and at construction from an
existing object, which is where shallow copies start to bite once [[Pointer]]s are involved.
See [[Copying]].
